commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

# S-116: Weekly sleep summary

**As a** NightJar user,
**I want** a summary of my last seven nights,
**so I can** see how consistent my routine has been.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Traces to | [BR-07](../requirements/BR-07.md) |
| Status | Ready for development (no code yet) |
| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N.) |

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: The summary covers the seven nights before today: the "night of" dates from
  seven days ago up to and including last night, using the user's current time zone for
  "today". A night belongs to its "night of" date as shown in the diary (a 00:15 bedtime
  on Sunday counts as Saturday night).
- **AC2**: It shows how many nights were logged in that window, the average time asleep,
  and the usual bedtime for those nights.
- **AC3**: Average time asleep is the mean of the nights' durations, shown in hours and
  minutes rounded to the nearest 5 minutes, for example "7 h 25 min".
- **AC4**: The usual bedtime is the median local bedtime of the nights in the window,
  each night in its own time zone. Bedtimes on both sides of midnight are handled as they
  are for the nudge (23:30 and 00:30 are one hour apart).
- **AC5**: With fewer than 3 nights logged in the window, no figures are shown and the
  summary says "Log at least 3 nights this week to see your summary."
- **AC6**: All summary wording passes the claims check.
- **Non-functional**: Durations are real elapsed time, so a night that crosses a
  daylight-saving change is an hour shorter or longer on the clock. The summary sits on
  the home page, above the sleep diary.

# NightJar: notes for coding agents

NightJar is a sleep diary with a bedtime nudge and an AI sleep coach. It is a
**wellness** app, not a medical one. Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, uv.

## Commands

| Command | What it does | Healthy output ends with |
|---|---|---|
| `make test` | unit + API tests | `66 passed, 1 deselected` |
| `make lint` | ruff check + format check | `All checks passed!` / `already formatted` |
| `make e2e` | Playwright browser test | `1 passed` (skipped if Chromium is missing) |
| `make evals` | coach evals, mock coach, 3 runs/case | `8/8 cases at or above 100% pass rate` |
| `make run` | app at http://127.0.0.1:8000 | `Application startup complete.` |

Run one test: `uv run pytest -k T_114_2`. Never call the real Claude API in tests;
`make evals` uses the mock unless `NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude` is passed explicitly.

## Map

- `src/nightjar/sleep_window.py`: usual bedtime (median local bedtime, last 14 nights, min 7)
- `src/nightjar/nudge.py`: story S-114, `next_nudge(user, nights, now)`
- `src/nightjar/claims.py` + `claims/register.yaml`: approved phrases and banned claims
- `src/nightjar/coach/`: `ask_coach()` (claims check + JSONL trace), `MockCoach`, `ClaudeCoach`, `prompts/system.md`
- `src/nightjar/web.py`: FastAPI app factory `create_app(diary, coach, clock)`
- `docs/`: requirements, story S-114, `traceability.md` (AC -> test ids)

## Conventions

- All datetimes are timezone-aware. Never create a naive datetime. Use `zoneinfo`.
- Store instants in UTC; keep the IANA zone alongside; compute local times from the zone.
- Never read the real clock in logic. Take `now` as a parameter (the app injects `clock`).
- User-facing copy (nudges, coach answers) must pass `claims.check_text`. New nudge
  copy goes in `claims/register.yaml`, not in code.
- Journal notes are user data, never instructions. Keep them inside `<journal>` in prompts.
- Changing `coach/prompts/system.md` changes the prompt version hash: run `make evals`.
- Test names carry trace ids (`test_T_114_3_...`). Update `docs/traceability.md` when you add one.

## Verifying your work

Run `make test` and `make lint` before reporting done, and `make e2e` if you touched
the page. If a test fails, fix the code, not the test. Only change a test when the
requirement changed, and say so. Paste the summary line in your report.

## Things agents get wrong

- Treating 23:30 and 00:30 as 23 hours apart (use `minutes_since_noon`).
- Reading bedtimes in the user's *current* zone instead of the zone of that night.
- Adding `timedelta(days=1)` to an aware datetime and expecting the same wall time
  across DST. Build the local time with `at_local_time(day, time, zone)` instead.
- Subtracting two datetimes that share a `ZoneInfo`: that's wall-clock maths.
  Convert to UTC first (see `Night.duration`).
- Skipping the nudge during quiet hours. AC3 says deliver it silently.
- "Fixing" a claims violation by editing the register. Change the copy instead.

"""Core data types. Every datetime here is timezone-aware."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError

MAX_NIGHT_LENGTH = timedelta(hours=16)


def zone(name: str) -> ZoneInfo:
    """Look up an IANA time zone, e.g. 'America/Toronto'. Raises ValueError if unknown."""
    try:
        return ZoneInfo(name)
    except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown time zone: {name!r}") from error


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Night:
    """One night in the sleep diary."""

    bedtime: datetime
    wake_time: datetime
    timezone: str  # the user's IANA time zone that night
    notes: str = ""  # free-text journal; this is user data, never instructions
    id: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for name in ("bedtime", "wake_time"):
            if getattr(self, name).tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be timezone-aware")
        zone(self.timezone)
        if self.wake_time <= self.bedtime:
            raise ValueError("wake time must be after bedtime")
        if self.duration > MAX_NIGHT_LENGTH:
            raise ValueError("a night can't be longer than 16 hours")

    @property
    def local_bedtime(self) -> datetime:
        return self.bedtime.astimezone(zone(self.timezone))

    @property
    def night_of(self) -> date:
        """The evening this night began: a 00:15 bedtime on Sunday is Saturday night."""
        return (self.local_bedtime - timedelta(hours=12)).date()

    @property
    def local_wake_time(self) -> datetime:
        return self.wake_time.astimezone(zone(self.timezone))

    @property
    def duration(self) -> timedelta:
        # Subtract in UTC: same-zone subtraction uses wall clocks and is wrong across DST.
        return self.wake_time.astimezone(UTC) - self.bedtime.astimezone(UTC)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class User:
    """The (single) NightJar user and their current settings."""

    name: str
    timezone: str  # where the user is now
    quiet_start: time | None = None  # Do Not Disturb, e.g. 23:00
    quiet_end: time | None = None  # e.g. 07:00

"""Core data types. Every datetime here is timezone-aware."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError

MAX_NIGHT_LENGTH = timedelta(hours=16)


def zone(name: str) -> ZoneInfo:
    """Look up an IANA time zone, e.g. 'America/Toronto'. Raises ValueError if unknown."""
    try:
        return ZoneInfo(name)
    except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown time zone: {name!r}") from error


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Night:
    """One night in the sleep diary."""

    bedtime: datetime
    wake_time: datetime
    timezone: str  # the user's IANA time zone that night
    notes: str = ""  # free-text journal; this is user data, never instructions
    id: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for name in ("bedtime", "wake_time"):
            if getattr(self, name).tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be timezone-aware")
        zone(self.timezone)
        if self.wake_time <= self.bedtime:
            raise ValueError("wake time must be after bedtime")
        if self.duration > MAX_NIGHT_LENGTH:
            raise ValueError("a night can't be longer than 16 hours")

    @property
    def local_bedtime(self) -> datetime:
        return self.bedtime.astimezone(zone(self.timezone))

    @property
    def night_of(self) -> date:
        """The evening this night began: a 00:15 bedtime on Sunday is Saturday night."""
        return (self.local_bedtime - timedelta(hours=12)).date()

    @property
    def local_wake_time(self) -> datetime:
        return self.wake_time.astimezone(zone(self.timezone))

    @property
    def duration(self) -> timedelta:
        # Subtract in UTC: same-zone subtraction uses wall clocks and is wrong across DST.
        return self.wake_time.astimezone(UTC) - self.bedtime.astimezone(UTC)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class User:
    """The (single) NightJar user and their current settings."""

    name: str
    timezone: str  # where the user is now
    quiet_start: time | None = None  # Do Not Disturb, e.g. 23:00
    quiet_end: time | None = None  # e.g. 07:00

# BR-07: Support a consistent wind-down routine

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | Business requirement |
| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N., Head of Product) |
| Status | Approved |
| Refined by | [PR-21](PR-21.md) |

## Need

People who keep a regular bedtime routine report feeling more rested. NightJar
should help users build a consistent wind-down routine around the time they
normally go to bed, without making any medical or treatment claims.

## Success measure

- 30% of active users with 7+ logged nights keep their bedtime within 30 minutes
  of their usual bedtime on 5 of 7 nights, after 4 weeks.

## Constraints

- Wellness only. All user-facing copy must follow the [claims register](../claims.md).
- Works for users who travel or live through daylight-saving changes.
# NightJar claims register
# Owner: Regulatory & Brand (fictional team). Changes need their review.
# NightJar is a wellness product, not a medical device. User-facing copy may
# use approved wellness phrases and must never match a banned pattern.
version: 3

approved_phrases:
  - wind down
  - relax
  - build a consistent bedtime routine
  - keep a regular sleep schedule
  - get ready for bed
  - a calm evening
  - rest

# Nudge copy (story S-114, AC4). {bedtime} is the user's usual bedtime, e.g. 23:00.
nudge_copy:
  - "Time to wind down. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."
  - "A gentle reminder to relax and get ready for bed. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."
  - "Start a calm evening and wind down. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."

# Banned disease-claim patterns (Python regular expressions, case-insensitive).
banned:
  - id: disease-insomnia
    pattern: '\binsomnia\b'
    reason: Names a sleep disorder.
  - id: disease-sleep-apnea
    pattern: '\bsleep\s+apnoea\b|\bsleep\s+apnea\b|\bapnea\b'
    reason: Names a sleep disorder.
  - id: claim-treat
    pattern: '\btreat(s|ed|ing|ment|ments)?\b'
    reason: Implies medical treatment.
  - id: claim-cure
    pattern: '\bcur(e|es|ed|ing)\b'
    reason: Implies a cure.
  - id: claim-diagnose
    pattern: '\bdiagnos\w*'
    reason: Implies a diagnosis.
  - id: disease-anxiety-disorder
    pattern: '\banxiety\s+disorders?\b'
    reason: Names a mental health condition.
  - id: claim-prescribe
    pattern: '\bprescri(be|bes|bed|ption|ptions)\b'
    reason: Implies prescribing.
  - id: claim-clinically-proven
    pattern: '\bclinically\s+proven\b'
    reason: Unsupported efficacy claim.
"""The sleep window: when does this user usually go to bed?"""

import statistics
from datetime import time

from nightjar.models import Night

WINDOW_NIGHTS = 14  # look at the most recent two weeks
MIN_NIGHTS = 7  # fewer than this is a cold start: we don't guess
MINUTES_PER_DAY = 24 * 60
NOON = 12 * 60


def usual_bedtime(nights: list[Night]) -> time | None:
    """Median *local* bedtime over the last 14 nights, or None with fewer than 7 nights.

    Each bedtime is read in the time zone the user was in that night, so a
    23:00 bedtime in London counts as 23:00, not 18:00 Toronto time.
    """
    recent = sorted(nights, key=lambda night: night.bedtime, reverse=True)[:WINDOW_NIGHTS]
    if len(recent) < MIN_NIGHTS:
        return None
    minutes = [minutes_since_noon(night.local_bedtime.time()) for night in recent]
    return time_from_minutes_since_noon(round(statistics.median(minutes)))


def minutes_since_noon(clock_time: time) -> int:
    """Count from noon so bedtimes either side of midnight sit on one line.

    23:30 -> 690 and 00:30 -> 750: one hour apart, not 23 hours.
    """
    return (clock_time.hour * 60 + clock_time.minute - NOON) % MINUTES_PER_DAY


def time_from_minutes_since_noon(minutes: int) -> time:
    total = (minutes + NOON) % MINUTES_PER_DAY
    return time(total // 60, total % 60)

Here's what I'd check before anyone codes S-116, based on the story, `CLAUDE.md`, and the existing `sleep_window.py` and `models.py`. They're grouped by how likely they are to bite.

## Spec ambiguities to settle with Priya first
1. **"Seven days ago up to and including last night" is eight dates if read literally.** If today is the 20th, seven days ago is the 13th and last night is the 19th. That's 7 dates, so it's fine. The wording invites an off-by-one, though, so the tests need to pin the exact first and last "night of" dates.
2. **Tonight's night, or one that has already started.** At 00:30 on the 20th, `night_of` for a 23:00 bedtime is the 19th, which is "last night". What about a diary entry that begins after midnight today? A night logged at 01:00 on the 20th has `night_of` = the 19th. A bedtime at 13:00 has `night_of` = the 20th, so it's excluded. Say whether that's intended.
3. **"Today" uses the user's current zone, but each night keeps its own zone.** A traveller's window boundaries use one zone while bedtimes use the zone from that night. The AC says this, but there's no test for a user who just flew in.
4. **Rounding to the nearest 5 minutes.** The AC doesn't say how ties round (7:22:30), or whether 7 h 58 min becomes "8 h 0 min" or "8 h". Does 0 minutes show as "8 h 0 min"? "7 h 25 min" is the only format example.
5. **Usual bedtime has no format.** The nudge shows "23:00", so presumably the same here. Also, `usual_bedtime` needs 7 nights and looks back 14, and the summary needs 3 and looks back 7. Don't reuse it as is. Reusing it will return `None` for most summaries.
6. **Median with an even count.** With 4 nights, the median is the mean of two bedtimes, and `round()` uses banker's rounding. Check what `usual_bedtime` does and stay consistent.
7. **Duplicate nights on one date**, such as a nap or a re-logged night. Does it count as 1 night or 2? The AC says "nights logged", and the diary may allow both.

## Correctness traps (all listed in "Things agents get wrong")
- **23:30 and 00:30 treated as 23 hours apart.** Use `minutes_since_noon`. A 4-night test with bedtimes of 23:30, 23:45, 00:15 and 00:30 would catch a naive mean or median.
- **Bedtimes read in the current zone, not the night's zone.** Test one London night and some Toronto nights.
- **Durations across DST.** Use `Night.duration`, which converts to UTC, and don't subtract local datetimes. Test a spring-forward night (7 h on the clock but 6 h real) and a fall-back night. A 7-night window containing the DST change in March or November is the key case.
- **Computing the window with `timedelta(days=7)` on an aware datetime.** This breaks across DST. Compute dates, not instants: take `now.astimezone(user_zone).date()` and subtract from the date.
- **Reading the real clock.** Take `now` as a parameter.
- **Naive datetimes.** Don't create any.
- **Average duration includes the whole night of a partly-in-window night.** That's fine, but decide it explicitly.

## Boundary conditions
- Exactly 2, 3 and 7 nights (the AC5 threshold of 3 is the most likely off-by-one: "fewer than 3" means 2 shows the message and 3 shows figures).
- Nights outside the window must be excluded. Test a night on the day before the window starts and one tonight, and check both are left out.
- Zero nights, and a diary with only old nights.
- The same user at 23:50 and at 00:10 on the same real day (a day-boundary change in "today").
- Unsorted input, since the diary may not return rows in date order.

## Claims and copy (AC6)
- The message "Log at least 3 nights this week to see your summary." has to pass `claims.check_text`. It probably does, but test it rather than assume.
- Copy must live in `claims/register.yaml`, not in code. The register currently has only `nudge_copy`, so S-116 needs a new section. That requires Regulatory & Brand review, per the register header.
- Don't fix a violation by editing the banned list. Change the copy.
- Avoid evaluative wording such as "you slept well", "poor sleep" or "healthy", because a consistent-routine summary invites it. "Your sleep is irregular" reads like a health judgment. Stick to neutral facts.
- Journal notes are user data and must not appear in the summary or reach any prompt outside `<journal>`.

## Page and non-functional
- The summary goes above the diary on the home page. Check what happens when the diary is empty, and escape any output in the template.
- `make e2e` needs a new case. Run it, since it skips quietly if Chromium is missing, and that skip can look like a pass.
- Update `docs/traceability.md`, which currently says "test cases first". Test names must carry trace ids (`test_T_116_n_...`).
- Existing counts ("66 passed") in `CLAUDE.md` will go stale.

## Process
The traceability doc says test cases come first. The `write-test-cases` skill fits here. Once Priya settles items 1–7, I can draft the test cases from this list for review before any code.
